newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on hedges, drop in CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on hedges, drop in CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on local and hedge selling and lower CBOT soy values, traders said.

"There were closing hedges in the May and July, there was a late break in the soybeans. There was local long liquidation and Japanese buying of the May at the close," a trader said. May WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -14.37 Friday from -13.53 Thursday. July-Nov spread at $58.50. Volume was 4,305 lots, or 86,100 tonnes, with 430 hedges.
May canola fell $4.60 to $424.50, July lost $4.50 to $427. May flax lost $0.80 to $360.20, November fell $1 to $327 met with scale-down commercial demand. Oats did not trade.
UGG bought 100 December feed pea contracts down US$1 at US$190 from a commercial, traders said.
May barley lost $2 to $142.50 on heavy hedges, 100 hedges were ordered at $143, a commission house said. July lost $1.60 to $140.90. May-July spread $1.50. Volume was 1,200 lots.
May feed wheat fell $2.30 at $172 with October up $0.80 to $169 on commercial demand, a trader said. May-Dec spread at $6, July-Dec $2, 100 Dec-Mar $3. Volume was 1,320 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
